{{Short description|Arithmetical function}}
In [[number theory]], '''Jordan's totient function''', denoted as <math>J_k(n)</math>, where <math>k</math> is a positive integer, is a function of a [[positive integer]], <math>n</math>, that equals the number of <math>k</math>-[[tuple]]s of positive integers that are less than or equal to <math>n</math> and that together with <math>n</math> form a [[Coprime integers#Coprimality in sets|coprime set]] of <math>k+1</math> integers.

Jordan's totient function is a generalization of [[Euler's totient function]], which is the same as <math>J_1(n)</math>. The function is named after [[Camille Jordan]].

==Definition==

For each positive integer <math>k</math>, Jordan's totient function <math>J_k</math> is [[multiplicative function|multiplicative]] and may be evaluated as
:<math>J_k(n)=n^k \prod_{p|n}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^k}\right) \,</math>, where <math>p</math> ranges through the prime divisors of <math>n</math>.

==Properties==

* <math>\sum_{d | n } J_k(d) = n^k. \, </math>
:which may be written in the language of [[Dirichlet convolution]]s as<ref>Sándor & Crstici (2004) p.106</ref>
:: <math>J_k(n) \star 1 = n^k\,</math>
:and via [[Möbius inversion formula|Möbius inversion]] as
::<math>J_k(n) = \mu(n) \star n^k</math>.
:Since the [[Dirichlet generating function]] of <math>\mu</math> is <math>1/\zeta(s)</math> and the Dirichlet generating function of <math>n^k</math> is <math>\zeta(s-k)</math>, the series for <math>J_k</math> becomes
::<math>\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{J_k(n)}{n^s} = \frac{\zeta(s-k)}{\zeta(s)}</math>.

* An [[Average order of an arithmetic function|average order]] of <math>J_k(n)</math> is  
::<math> J_k(n) \sim \frac{n^k}{\zeta(k+1)}</math>.

* The [[Dedekind psi function]] is
::<math>\psi(n) = \frac{J_2(n)}{J_1(n)}</math>,
:and by inspection of the definition (recognizing that each factor in the product over the primes is a cyclotomic polynomial of <math>p^{-k}</math>), the arithmetic functions defined by <math>\frac{J_k(n)}{J_1(n)}</math> or <math>\frac{J_{2k}(n)}{J_k(n)}</math> can also be shown to be integer-valued multiplicative functions.

* <math>\sum_{\delta\mid n}\delta^sJ_r(\delta)J_s\left(\frac{n}{\delta}\right) = J_{r+s}(n)</math>.<ref>Holden ''et al'' in external links. The formula is Gegenbauer's.</ref>

==Order of matrix groups==

* The [[general linear group]] of matrices of order <math>m</math> over <math>\mathbf{Z}/n</math> has order<ref>All of these formulas are from Andrica and Piticari in [[#External links]].</ref>
:<math>
|\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbf{Z}/n)|=n^{\frac{m(m-1)}{2}}\prod_{k=1}^m J_k(n).
</math>

* The [[special linear group]] of matrices of order <math>m</math> over <math>\mathbf{Z}/n</math> has order
:<math>
|\operatorname{SL}(m,\mathbf{Z}/n)|=n^{\frac{m(m-1)}{2}}\prod_{k=2}^m J_k(n).
</math>

* The [[symplectic group]] of matrices of order <math>m</math> over <math>\mathbf{Z}/n</math> has order
:<math>
|\operatorname{Sp}(2m,\mathbf{Z}/n)|=n^{m^2}\prod_{k=1}^m J_{2k}(n).
</math>

The first two formulas were discovered by Jordan.

==Examples==

* Explicit lists in the [[OEIS]] are J<sub>2</sub> in {{OEIS2C|A007434}}, J<sub>3</sub> in {{OEIS2C|A059376}}, J<sub>4</sub> in {{OEIS2C|A059377}}, J<sub>5</sub> in {{OEIS2C|A059378}}, J<sub>6</sub> up to J<sub>10</sub> in {{OEIS2C|A069091}} up to {{OEIS2C|A069095}}.
* Multiplicative functions defined by ratios are J<sub>2</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A001615}}, J<sub>3</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160889}}, J<sub>4</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160891}}, J<sub>5</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160893}}, J<sub>6</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160895}}, J<sub>7</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160897}}, J<sub>8</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160908}}, J<sub>9</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160953}}, J<sub>10</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160957}}, J<sub>11</sub>(n)/J<sub>1</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A160960}}.
* Examples of the ratios J<sub>2k</sub>(n)/J<sub>k</sub>(n) are J<sub>4</sub>(n)/J<sub>2</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A065958}}, J<sub>6</sub>(n)/J<sub>3</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A065959}}, and J<sub>8</sub>(n)/J<sub>4</sub>(n) in {{OEIS2C|A065960}}.
